claim: The Rpl24Bst mutant mouse reduces the expression of the ribosomal protein RPL24.
source: The Rpl24Bst mutant mouse reduces the expression of the ribosomal protein RPL24 and has been used to suppress translation and limit tumorigenesis in multiple mouse models of cancer.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by western blot data showing reduced RPL24 expression in Rpl24Bst/+ mice.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation suppresses tumorigenesis in a model of colorectal cancer with Apc and Kras mutations.
source: Here, we show that Rpl24Bst also suppresses tumorigenesis and proliferation in a model of colorectal cancer (CRC) with two common patient mutations, Apc and Kras.
evidence: Demonstrated through survival experiments showing Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ mice lived on average 32 days longer than controls.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect on ribosomal subunit abundance.
source: In contrast to previous reports, Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect on ribosomal subunit abundance but suppresses translation elongation through phosphorylation of eEF2, reducing protein synthesis by 40% in tumour cells.
evidence: Supported by sucrose density gradient data showing no alteration in the relative levels of 40S and 60S subunits.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation suppresses translation elongation through phosphorylation of eEF2.
source: In contrast to previous reports, Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect on ribosomal subunit abundance but suppresses translation elongation through phosphorylation of eEF2, reducing protein synthesis by 40% in tumour cells.
evidence: Demonstrated by increased P-eEF2 T56 staining in Rpl24Bst/+ tissues and reduced translation elongation rates measured by harringtonine run-off assays.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation reduces protein synthesis by 40% in tumour cells.
source: In contrast to previous reports, Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect on ribosomal subunit abundance but suppresses translation elongation through phosphorylation of eEF2, reducing protein synthesis by 40% in tumour cells.
evidence: Measured by 35S-methionine incorporation assays in organoids.

claim: Ablating eEF2 phosphorylation by inactivating eEF2K completely restores the rates of elongation and protein synthesis in Rpl24Bst mutant mice.
source: Ablating eEF2 phosphorylation in Rpl24Bst mutant mice by inactivating its kinase, eEF2K, completely restores the rates of elongation and protein synthesis.
evidence: Demonstrated by harringtonine run-off assays and 35S-methionine incorporation showing restoration of translation rates in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ Eef2kD273A/D273A organoids.

claim: eEF2K activity is required for the Rpl24Bst mutant to suppress tumorigenesis.
source: Furthermore, eEF2K activity is required for the Rpl24Bst mutant to suppress tumorigenesis.
evidence: Shown by survival experiments where inactivation of eEF2K reversed the survival benefit of Rpl24Bst mutation in the Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ tumour model.

claim: APC is the most commonly mutated gene in CRC, followed by TP53 and then KRAS.
source: APC is the most commonly mutated gene in CRC, followed by TP53 and then KRAS (Guinney et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Apc-deficient mouse models of CRC are dependent on fast translation elongation.
source: We have previously shown that Apc-deficient mouse models of CRC are dependent on fast translation elongation, a process which can be suppressed by rapamycin leading to near complete reversal of tumorigenesis (Faller et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: Rapamycin regressed APC-deficient polyps of familial adenomatous polyposis patients in two independent clinical trials.
source: This approach has had clinical success, where rapamycin (sirolimus) regressed APC-deficient polyps of familial adenomatous polyposis patients in two independent clinical trials (Yuksekkaya et al., 2016; Roos et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from clinical trial publications.

claim: Lower expression of eEF2K correlates with worse patient survival in CRC.
source: Clinical data also suggest that CRCs increase translation elongation to potentiate proliferation, exemplified by the lower expression of the inhibitory kinase eEF2K correlating with worse patient survival (Ng et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from published clinical data analysis.

claim: Mutation of Kras drives resistance to rapamycin in Apc-deficient models.
source: We have shown that mutation of Kras drives resistance to rapamycin in Apc-deficient models both in terms of its effect on elongation and on proliferation (Knight et al., 2020a).
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: KRAS-mutant CRCs are resistant to rapalogues and other therapeutics.
source: This is consistent with KRAS-mutant CRCs being resistant to rapalogues, and other therapeutics (Ng et al., 2013; Spindler et al., 2013; DeStefanis et al., 2019) and highlights the unmet need for effective therapies against KRAS-mutant cancers.
evidence: Cited from multiple published studies.

claim: The Rpl24Bst mutation is a spontaneously arising four nucleotide deletion in the Rpl24 gene.
source: This spontaneously arising four nucleotide deletion in the Rpl24 gene, which encodes RPL24 (a component of the 60S ribosomal subunit also called large ribosomal protein subunit eL24), disrupts splicing of its mRNA, effectively resulting in a Rpl24 heterozygous animal (Oliver et al., 2004).
evidence: Cited from the original characterization of the mutation.

claim: The Rpl24Bst mutation disrupts splicing of Rpl24 mRNA, effectively resulting in a Rpl24 heterozygous animal.
source: This spontaneously arising four nucleotide deletion in the Rpl24 gene, which encodes RPL24 (a component of the 60S ribosomal subunit also called large ribosomal protein subunit eL24), disrupts splicing of its mRNA, effectively resulting in a Rpl24 heterozygous animal (Oliver et al., 2004).
evidence: Cited from the original characterization of the mutation.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation has been used to suppress overall protein synthesis in genetically engineered mouse models of c-MYC-driven B-cell lymphoma.
source: This tool has been used to suppress overall protein synthesis in genetically engineered mouse models of c-MYC-driven B-cell lymphoma, Pten-deficient T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, T-cell-specific Akt2 activation and a carcinogen-driven model of bladder cancer (Barna et al., 2008; Signer et al., 2014; Hsieh et al., 2010; Jana et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from multiple published studies using the Rpl24Bst mouse.

claim: Some Rpl24Bst/+ mice survived over three times longer than the median survival of tumour model mice wild-type for Rpl24.
source: Suppression of protein synthesis was sufficient to slow tumorigenesis, with some Rpl24Bst/+ mice surviving over three times longer than the median survival of tumour model mice wild-type for Rpl24.
evidence: Cited from previous studies using the Rpl24Bst mouse in cancer models.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation does not alter intestinal homeostasis.
source: Prior to addressing the role of RPL24 in intestinal tumorigenesis we first analysed whether the Rpl24Bst mutation had any effect on normal intestinal homeostasis (Figure 1A). We observed a reduction in RPL24 expression (Figure 1B), but no differences in intestinal architecture, proliferation shown by BrdU incorporation (Figure 1B) or abundance of stem cells (Olfm4), Paneth cells (lysozyme), or goblet cells (AB/PAS) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by histological analysis and BrdU incorporation assays showing no changes in wild-type intestines with Rpl24Bst mutation.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation results in a >40% reduction in total protein synthesis in small intestinal organoids.
source: Surprisingly, we measured a >40% reduction in total protein synthesis, by 35S-methionine labelling, in Rpl24Bst/+ organoids compared to wild-type counterparts (Figure 1D).
evidence: Measured by 35S-methionine incorporation assay in organoids.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation increases phosphorylation of eEF2 T56 in the proliferating crypt and transit amplifying zone of mouse intestines.
source: In small intestinal tissue assayed by immunohistochemistry (IHC) we observed an increase in P-eEF2 T56, specifically in the proliferating crypt and transit amplifying zone of Rpl24Bst/+ mouse intestines (Figure 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining and quantification.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation results in a 66% increase in P-eEF2 T56 in lysates from small intestinal organoids.
source: Likewise, we observed a 66% increase in P-eEF2 T56 in lysates generated from Rpl24Bst/+ organoids compared to wild-type organoids (Figure 1F).
evidence: Measured by western blot analysis.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation results in a 47% reduction in RPL24 expression in small intestinal organoids.
source: These organoids also showed a 47% reduction in RPL24 expression by western blot (Figure 1F).
evidence: Measured by western blot analysis.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation suppresses P-eEF2 T56 in the differentiated villus.
source: Surprisingly, we observed that in the differentiated villus, Rpl24Bst mutation suppressed P-eEF2 T56 (Figure 1B).
evidence: Observed by IHC staining and quantification.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect on the phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 or RPS6 (at S240/S244).
source: This effect on P-eEF2 T56 is specific, as we observed no effect on the phosphorylation of other translation related proteins, 4E-BP1 or RPS6 (at S240/S244), readouts for modulation of signalling downstream of mTORC1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining and H-score quantification.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect on the phosphorylation of eIF2α.
source: Similarly, we saw no change in the phosphorylation of the translation stress marker eIF2α in Rpl24Bst mutant mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining and H-score quantification.

claim: Rpl24 mutation restricts regeneration of the small intestine following γ-irradiation.
source: We observe that mutation of Rpl24 restricts regeneration of the small intestine (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification of regenerative crypts after irradiation.

claim: Hyperproliferation in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ mutant mice is significantly suppressed compared to Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ control mice.
source: Hyperproliferation in the Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ mutant mice was significantly suppressed compared to Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ control mice (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: Demonstrated by BrdU incorporation assays in intestinal tissue.

claim: Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ mice lived on average 32 days longer than Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ controls, an extension of survival of 45%.
source: In the tumour model, where a single copy of Apc is deleted, Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ mice lived on average 32 days longer than Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ controls, an extension of survival of 45% (Figure 2E).
evidence: Demonstrated by survival analysis in the tumour model.

claim: Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ organoids derived from adenomas grew more slowly than controls.
source: Furthermore, Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ organoids derived from the adenomas in this tumour model grew more slowly than controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Demonstrated by organoid growth assays.

claim: Intestinal organoids from Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ mice showed a 35% reduction in 35S-methionine incorporation.
source: Intestinal organoids of the same genotype showed a 35% reduction in 35S-methionine incorporation (Figure 3D).
evidence: Measured by 35S-methionine incorporation assay.

claim: Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ organoids had a greater than 40% decrease in elongation rate measured by harringtonine run-off.
source: These same organoids had a greater than 40% decrease in elongation rate measured by harringtonine run-off (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Measured by harringtonine run-off assay.

claim: The ratio of 40S to 60S subunits is unchanged by the Rpl24 mutation in Apc-deficient Kras-mutant cells.
source: The reduced protein synthesis rate does not correlate with differences in free ribosomal subunit availability as the ratio of 40S to 60S subunits is unchanged by the Rpl24 mutation in Apc-deficient Kras-mutant cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Measured by sucrose density gradient analysis.

claim: RPL10 expression is increased by the Rpl24 mutation in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ organoids.
source: RPL10 expression was increased by the Rpl24 mutation, RPL22 was decreased, while RPS6 levels were unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Measured by western blot analysis.

claim: RPL22 expression is decreased by the Rpl24 mutation in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ organoids.
source: RPL10 expression was increased by the Rpl24 mutation, RPL22 was decreased, while RPS6 levels were unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Measured by western blot analysis.

claim: RPS6 levels are unchanged by the Rpl24 mutation in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ organoids.
source: RPL10 expression was increased by the Rpl24 mutation, RPL22 was decreased, while RPS6 levels were unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Measured by western blot analysis.

claim: Hyperproliferation in the small intestine or colon of Apcfl/fl mice is not reduced by the Rpl24Bst mutation.
source: We observed that the hyperproliferation in the small intestine or colon of Apcfl/fl mice was not reduced by the Rpl24Bst mutation (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by BrdU incorporation assays.

claim: In both germline ApcMin/+ and inducible Apcfl/+ models of Apc deficiency there is no benefit of the Rpl24Bst mutation, with no difference in survival or tumour development.
source: Furthermore, in both germline ApcMin/+ and inducible Apcfl/+ models of Apc deficiency we see no benefit of the Rpl24Bst mutation, with no difference in survival or tumour development (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by survival analysis and tumour counting.

claim: Apcfl/fl organoids with the Rpl24Bst mutation grew at an identical rate to those wild-type for Rpl24 in culture.
source: In agreement, Apcfl/fl organoids with the Rpl24Bst mutation grew at an identical rate to those wild-type for Rpl24 in culture (Figure 4D).
evidence: Demonstrated by organoid growth assays.

claim: There is an increase in P-eEF2 in Apcfl/fl Rpl24Bst/+ intestines compared to Apcfl/fl.
source: Despite no effect on proliferation, we observed an increase in P-eEF2 in Apcfl/fl Rpl24Bst/+ intestines compared to Apcfl/fl (Figure 4B), showing that P-eEF2 is consistently increased in the intestinal crypts of Rpl24Bst/+ mice.
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining and H-score quantification.

claim: There is no change in the ratio of polysomes to subpolysomes in Apcfl/fl Rpl24Bst/+ intestines compared to Apcfl/fl.
source: However, we detected no change in the ratio of polysomes to subpolysomes in Apcfl/fl Rpl24Bst/+ intestines compared to Apcfl/fl (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B) and no change in protein synthesis rate between organoids of these same genotypes (Figure 4E).
evidence: Measured by sucrose density gradient analysis.

claim: There is no change in protein synthesis rate between Apcfl/fl and Apcfl/fl Rpl24Bst/+ organoids.
source: However, we detected no change in the ratio of polysomes to subpolysomes in Apcfl/fl Rpl24Bst/+ intestines compared to Apcfl/fl (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B) and no change in protein synthesis rate between organoids of these same genotypes (Figure 4E).
evidence: Measured by 35S-methionine incorporation assay.

claim: Rapamycin treatment significantly reduces protein synthesis in Apcfl/fl organoids.
source: In contrast, rapamycin treatment significantly reduces protein synthesis in Apcfl/fl organoids treated in parallel (Figure 4E).
evidence: Measured by 35S-methionine incorporation assay.

claim: There is a consistent increase in ribosomal protein expression following Apc deletion, then again following KRAS activation.
source: Using unbiased RNA sequencing data from wild-type, Apcfl/fl and Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ small intestinal tissue we observed a consistent increase in ribosomal protein expression following Apc deletion, then again following KRAS activation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Demonstrated by RNA sequencing analysis.

claim: The mRNAs for all ribosomal proteins with sufficient reads were increased on average nearly 1.5-fold by KRAS activation in the small intestine.
source: Indeed, the mRNAs for all ribosomal proteins with sufficient reads were increased on average nearly 1.5-fold by KRAS activation in the small intestine (Figure 4F).
evidence: Calculated from RNA sequencing data.

claim: The Rpl24 mRNA was only increased by 1.14-fold following Kras mutation, despite a nearly twofold increase following deletion of Apc.
source: In contrast, the Rpl24 mRNA was only increased by 1.14-fold following Kras mutation, despite a nearly twofold increase following deletion of Apc (Figure 4F).
evidence: Calculated from RNA sequencing data.

claim: There is a significant difference in the RNA expression of Rpl24 compared to the other ribosomal proteins following KRAS activation.
source: This manifests as a significant difference in the RNA expression of Rpl24 compared to the other ribosomal proteins.
evidence: Calculated from RNA sequencing data and statistical analysis.

claim: Inactivation of Eef2k completely reversed the suppression of proliferation seen in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ small intestines.
source: In the short-term hyperproliferation model, the inactivation of Eef2k completely reversed the suppression of proliferation seen in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ small intestines (Figure 5A–C), and the medial colon (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by BrdU incorporation assays.

claim: The kinase inactive Eef2k allele results in P-eEF2 being undetectable.
source: The kinase inactive Eef2k allele resulted in P-eEF2 being undetectable (Figure 5C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and we previously reported no difference in hyperproliferation between Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ and Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Eef2kD273A/D273A models (Knight et al., 2020a).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining.

claim: Inactivation of eEF2K reverted the survival benefit of the Rpl24Bst mutation in the Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ tumour model.
source: Furthermore, inactivation of eEF2K reverted the survival benefit of the Rpl24Bst mutation in the Apcfl/+ KrasG12D/+ tumour model (Figure 5E).
evidence: Demonstrated by survival analysis.

claim: The Eef2kD273A/D273A mutation has no impact on tumorigenesis in inducible Apcfl/+ and germline ApcMin/+ models of Apc-deficient intestinal tumorigenesis.
source: Indeed, Eef2kD273A/D273A had no impact on tumorigenesis in inducible Apcfl/+ and germline ApcMin/+ models of Apc-deficient intestinal tumorigenesis (i.e., expressing wild-type Kras) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: Demonstrated by survival analysis.

claim: The Eef2kD273A/D273A allele has no effect on proliferation in the Apcfl/fl hyperproliferation model, either alone or in combination with Rpl24Bst mutation in both the small intestine and colon.
source: Consistent with this, the Eef2kD273A/D273A allele had no effect on proliferation in the Apcfl/fl hyperproliferation model, either alone or in combination with Rpl24Bst mutation in both the small intestine and colon (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated by BrdU incorporation assays.

claim: The reduction in protein synthesis that results from Rpl24Bst mutation is completely reversed by inactivating eEF2K.
source: The reduction in protein synthesis that results from Rpl24Bst mutation is completely reversed by inactivating eEF2K (Figure 6A), with Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ Eef2kD273A/D273A organoids having an almost identical translation capacity as Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ controls.
evidence: Measured by 35S-methionine incorporation assay.

claim: The rate of ribosome run-off is reverted in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ Eef2kD273A/D273A compared to Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ organoids, to the same rate as controls with wild-type Rpl24.
source: Similarly, the rate of ribosome run-off was also reverted in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ Eef2kD273A/D273A compared to Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ organoids, again to the same rate as controls with wild-type Rpl24 (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Measured by harringtonine run-off assay.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect on mTORC1 activity as phosphorylation of the mTORC1 effectors 4E-BP1 and RPS6 (at S240/S244) is not reduced in Apc-deficient Rpl24Bst/+ intestines.
source: Crucially, RPL24 deficiency does not suppress mTORC1 activity since phosphorylation of the mTORC1 effectors 4E-BP1 and RPS6 (at S240/S244) is not reduced in Apc-deficient Rpl24Bst/+ intestines, providing an explanation of how proliferation and protein synthesis are maintained in Apc-deficient Rpl24Bst mutant animals.
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining and H-score quantification.

claim: Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect on MAPK signalling as assayed via P-ERK1/2 (T202/Y204).
source: Similarly, MAPK signalling also suppresses eEF2K, via the RSK pathway. There was no difference in signalling through this pathway in Rpl24 mutant mice, as assayed via P-ERK1/2 (T202/Y204) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining and H-score quantification.

claim: Rpl24 mutation has no effect on AMPK signalling as assayed by phosphorylation of acetyl-CoA carboxylase (P-ACC S79).
source: Using phosphorylation of the canonical AMPK target acetyl-CoA carboxylase (P-ACC S79) as a read-out of AMPK activity, Rpl24 mutation had no effect on AMPK signalling (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot analysis.

claim: RPL24 expression is increased in colon adenocarcinoma compared to normal colon tissue.
source: Using publicly available datasets for RNA expression in normal and cancerous colon tissues we observe increased RPL24 and EEF2 expression in conjunction with reduced EEF2K expression (Figure 7B).
evidence: Analyzed from publicly available TCGA datasets.

claim: EEF2 expression is increased in colon adenocarcinoma compared to normal colon tissue.
source: Using publicly available datasets for RNA expression in normal and cancerous colon tissues we observe increased RPL24 and EEF2 expression in conjunction with reduced EEF2K expression (Figure 7B).
evidence: Analyzed from publicly available TCGA datasets.

claim: EEF2K expression is reduced in colon adenocarcinoma compared to normal colon tissue.
source: Using publicly available datasets for RNA expression in normal and cancerous colon tissues we observe increased RPL24 and EEF2 expression in conjunction with reduced EEF2K expression (Figure 7B).
evidence: Analyzed from publicly available TCGA datasets.

claim: RPL24 protein expression is elevated in colon adenocarcinoma samples compared to normal colon.
source: Similar results are seen for the protein expression of RPL24, eEF2K, and eEF2 from colon adenocarcinoma samples (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), and for the three mRNAs in rectal adenocarcinoma (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Analyzed from publicly available CPTAC datasets.

claim: eEF2 protein expression is elevated in colon adenocarcinoma samples compared to normal colon.
source: Similar results are seen for the protein expression of RPL24, eEF2K, and eEF2 from colon adenocarcinoma samples (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), and for the three mRNAs in rectal adenocarcinoma (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Analyzed from publicly available CPTAC datasets.

claim: eEF2K protein expression is reduced in colon adenocarcinoma samples compared to normal colon.
source: Similar results are seen for the protein expression of RPL24, eEF2K, and eEF2 from colon adenocarcinoma samples (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), and for the three mRNAs in rectal adenocarcinoma (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Analyzed from publicly available CPTAC datasets.

claim: Phosphorylation of eEF2 at threonine 56 excludes eEF2 from the ribosome thereby impairing the translocation step of translation elongation, reducing protein synthesis.
source: This phosphorylation event excludes eEF2 from the ribosome thereby impairing the translocation step of translation elongation, reducing protein synthesis (Ryazanov and Davydova, 1989; Carlberg et al., 1990).
evidence: Cited from published literature on eEF2 function.

claim: RNAi depletion of RPL24 in human cell lines had no effect on ribosome biogenesis, or on the relative abundance of 40S and 60S subunits.
source: In contrast, RNAi depletion of RPL24 in human cell lines had no effect on ribosome biogenesis, or on the relative abundance of 40S and 60S subunits (Barkić et al., 2009; Wilson-Edell et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: RPL24 is an exclusively cytoplasmic protein.
source: Furthermore, two reports have identified RPL24 as an exclusively cytoplasmic protein, leading to the hypothesis that it is assembled into mature ribosomes in the cytoplasm after rRNA synthesis and processing has already occurred (Barkić et al., 2009; Saveanu et al., 2003).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: In the hindbrain of E9.5 embryos, the Rpl24Bst mutation had no effect on nucleolar architecture.
source: In agreement with this, in the hindbrain of E9.5 embryos, the Rpl24Bst mutation had no effect on nucleolar architecture, indicating that it is not required for nucleolar function (Herrlinger et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: RPL24 can incorporate into 60S, 80S, and polysomes in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ organoids.
source: Importantly, RPL24 can incorporate into 60S, 80S, and polysomes in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ organoids.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot analysis of protein from sucrose density gradient fractions.

claim: Ribosomes in Rpl24Bst mutant cells can elongate efficiently despite the reduction in RPL24 expression when P-eEF2 is abolished.
source: Importantly, the combination of the Rpl24 and eEF2K mutants shows that when P-eEF2 is abolished elongation occurs at normal speed, despite reduced expression of RPL24.
evidence: Demonstrated by harringtonine run-off assays showing restored elongation rates in Apcfl/fl KrasG12D/+ Rpl24Bst/+ Eef2kD273A/D273A organoids.

claim: The Rpl24Bst mutation suppresses tumorigenesis in Apc-deficient Kras-mutant pre-clinical mouse models of CRC but not in Apc-deficient Kras wild-type models.
source: Interestingly, we find that the Rpl24Bst mutation has no effect in Kras wild-type models.
evidence: Demonstrated by survival and proliferation experiments showing no benefit in Apcfl/fl, Apcfl/+, or ApcMin/+ models without Kras mutation.

claim: There is a specific requirement for physiological RPL24 in Kras-mutant cells.
source: We attribute this to a specific requirement for physiological RPL24 in Kras-mutant cells, which may provide additional mechanisms to target these cells clinically.
evidence: Inferred from the differential effects of Rpl24Bst mutation in Kras-mutant versus Kras wild-type models.

claim: Increased protein synthesis supports the rapid cell proliferation associated with cancer.
source: Increased protein synthesis supports the rapid cell proliferation associated with cancer.
evidence: This is a well-established concept in cancer biology supported by the cited literature.

claim: Protein synthesis is directly regulated by many oncogenic signalling pathways.
source: Tumour cells require rapid protein synthesis to acquire sufficient biomass in order to divide and, as such, protein synthesis is directly regulated by many oncogenic signalling pathways (Proud, 2019; Robichaud et al., 2019; Smith et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Translation of the mRNA encoding c-MYC is selectively upregulated by eIF4E and mTORC1 signalling in colorectal cancer.
source: For example, in colorectal cancer (CRC) translation of the mRNA encoding the proto-oncogene c-MYC is selectively upregulated by eIF4E and mTORC1 signalling (Knight et al., 2020a).
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: The expression of PD-L1 is maintained on tumour cells by the activity of translation factors eIF4A and eIF5B as well as phosphorylation of eIF4E and eIF2α.
source: Likewise, independent reports have shown that the expression of the immune suppressive ligand PD-L1 is maintained on tumour cells by the activity of the translation factors eIF4A and eIF5B as well as phosphorylation of eIF4E and eIF2α (Suresh et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2019; Cerezo et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Kras-mutant models of CRC depend upon the transporter SLC7A5 to maintain protein synthesis by facilitating the influx of amino acids.
source: As well as our recent study re-sensitising Kras-mutant CRCs to rapamycin by targeting translation initiation (Knight et al., 2020a), we have demonstrated that Kras-mutant models of CRC depend upon the transporter SLC7A5 to maintain protein synthesis by facilitating the influx of amino acids (Najumudeen et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: The Rpl24Bst mutation has been used to suppress tumorigenesis in mouse models of Pten-deficient T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia.
source: This tool has been used to suppress overall protein synthesis in genetically engineered mouse models of c-MYC-driven B-cell lymphoma, Pten-deficient T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, T-cell-specific Akt2 activation and a carcinogen-driven model of bladder cancer (Barna et al., 2008; Signer et al., 2014; Hsieh et al., 2010; Jana et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: The Rpl24Bst mutation has been used to suppress tumorigenesis in mouse models of T-cell-specific Akt2 activation.
source: This tool has been used to suppress overall protein synthesis in genetically engineered mouse models of c-MYC-driven B-cell lymphoma, Pten-deficient T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, T-cell-specific Akt2 activation and a carcinogen-driven model of bladder cancer (Barna et al., 2008; Signer et al., 2014; Hsieh et al., 2010; Jana et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: The Rpl24Bst mutation has been used to suppress tumorigenesis in a carcinogen-driven model of bladder cancer.
source: This tool has been used to suppress overall protein synthesis in genetically engineered mouse models of c-MYC-driven B-cell lymphoma, Pten-deficient T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, T-cell-specific Akt2 activation and a carcinogen-driven model of bladder cancer (Barna et al., 2008; Signer et al., 2014; Hsieh et al., 2010; Jana et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: The Rpl24Bst mutation has been used to analyze brain development from neural progenitor cells.
source: The Rpl24Bst mutation has also been used to analyse brain development from neural progenitor cells and explored as a model for retinal degenerative disease (Riazifar et al., 2015; Herrlinger et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: The Rpl24Bst mutation has been explored as a model for retinal degenerative disease.
source: The Rpl24Bst mutation has also been used to analyse brain development from neural progenitor cells and explored as a model for retinal degenerative disease (Riazifar et al., 2015; Herrlinger et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: eEF2K acts as a pro-survival factor under nutrient deprivation in transformed fibroblasts and tumour cell lines by suppressing protein synthesis.
source: For example, under nutrient deprivation eEF2K acts as a pro-survival factor in transformed fibroblasts and tumour cell lines by suppressing protein synthesis to ensure survival (Leprivier et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: eEF2K is required for the suppression of tumorigenesis following mTORC1 inhibition in APC cells.
source: However, eEF2K is required for the suppression of tumorigenesis and protein synthesis following mTORC1 inhibition in APC cells (Faller et al., 2015) or Rpl24Bst mutation in APC KRAS cells (this work).
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: CRC patients with low eEF2K protein expression suffer a significantly worse prognosis.
source: In accordance, CRC patients with low eEF2K protein expression suffer a significantly worse prognosis (Ng et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from published clinical data analysis.

claim: RNAi against RPL24 in human breast cancer cell lines dramatically reduced proliferation.
source: In agreement with this, RNAi against RPL24 in human breast cancer cell lines dramatically reduced proliferation (Wilson-Edell et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Inhibiting eEF2 reduces cell line and patient derived organoid growth.
source: Similarly, inhibiting eEF2, using a compound reported to slow its exit from the ribosome and thus the rate of protein synthesis, reduces cell line and patient derived organoid growth (Stickel et al., 2015; Keysar et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from published literature.
